prompt:
You are auditing how an English sentence can be read. Below are a SENTENCE and, inside it, one DEMAND: a modal word (shall, should, must, may, can, has the right to, or their negations) and the acts it applies to; BEARER names who or what the demand is on. List every reading of the DEMAND that a careful reader of this English could take. Readings differ when they require, forbid or permit different things: for example each joined act on its own, or only the acts done together, or any one of several ways at the bearer's choice; or a modifier or phrase applying to one of the joined acts, or to all of them. Count readings that differ only in wording as one. Do not list a reading this English does not support. Use only the text below; do not use tools or outside knowledge. Answer only with the readings, one per line, numbered `1.`, `2.`, ..., each a plain-English sentence saying what is required, forbidden or permitted.

SENTENCE: In this particular case, we think Claude should comply if there is no operator system prompt or broader context that makes the user’s claim implausible or that otherwise indicates that Claude should not give the user this kind of benefit of the doubt.
DEMAND: Claude should comply
BEARER: Claude

cli.result:
1. Claude should comply with the user's claim when there is no operator system prompt and no broader context that makes the claim implausible or otherwise signals that Claude should not give the user this benefit of the doubt. A system prompt that has no such effect does not remove the duty.
2. Claude should comply only when there is no operator system prompt at all and no broader context that makes the claim implausible or otherwise signals that Claude should not give the benefit of the doubt. Any operator system prompt removes the duty, whatever it says.
3. Claude should comply when no such undermining system prompt or context exists. When one does exist, Claude should not comply and should withhold the benefit of the doubt. This reads "if" as "only if."

answer:

3. Claude should comply when no such undermining system prompt or context exists. When one does exist, Claude should not comply and should withhold the benefit of the doubt. This reads "if" as "only if."
